subject: Accounting
title: Luckin Coffee's Fake Sales
description: Learn Luckin Coffee's Fake Sales in one minute.

hook.text: Luckin Coffee claimed to rival Starbucks in China. Half its sales were invented.

buildup.text: The company fabricated $310 million in revenue through fake customer transactions.

discovery.text: A short seller published a report with video evidence of empty stores claiming busy traffic.

twist.text: Luckin was listed on NASDAQ—American investors lost billions in a Chinese fraud.

climax.text: Luckin was delisted, fined $180 million, and forced to restructure entirely.

punchline.text: Video cameras caught what auditors missed.

quiz.question: How was Luckin Coffee's fraud exposed?
options: A short seller published video evidence of empty stores

details.summary: Luckin Coffee, China's answer to Starbucks, fabricated $310 million in sales to appear far more successful than it was. This topic covers how employees manufactured fake transactions, how short sellers exposed the fraud, and the implications for Chinese companies listed in the US.
details.whyItMatters: Luckin Coffee accelerated US legislative action requiring foreign companies to comply with American audit oversight, fundamentally changing the landscape for Chinese firms listed on American stock exchanges.
takeaways: Luckin fabricated roughly 40% of its sales in 2019 through fake corporate bulk purchases
Short seller Muddy Waters published research exposing inflated store traffic and fake receipts
The fraud led directly to the Holding Foreign Companies Accountable Act in the US

faq.question: How did Luckin Coffee fake its sales?
faq.answer: Luckin inflated 2019 sales by roughly $310 million—about 40% of reported revenue—through fabricated corporate bulk purchase orders, inflated per-store sales, and overstated customer counts. Employees created fake vouchers and routed money through related parties to simulate real transactions.

faq.question: How was the Luckin Coffee fraud discovered?
faq.answer: Short seller Muddy Waters published a damning report based on 11,260 hours of in-store video surveillance and thousands of scraped receipts showing actual sales were far below reported figures. Luckin later confirmed the fraud in an internal investigation.
